'''Shooting Stars''' is a [[Distraction and Diversion]] activity in which players mine [[crashed star]]s for [[stardust]]. A star will crash roughly every 90 minutes on each [[server]] (with a variation of up to 15 minutes), falling at a random spot selected from a predetermined list. The activity is notable for providing idle [[Mining]] training, only requiring input every 7 minutes while mining a star.

Stardust may be exchanged at [[Dusuri's Star Shop]] by the [[Mining Guild]] entrance in [[Falador]] for various [[Shooting Stars#Rewards|rewards]]. Although the activity is available in [[Free-to-play]], players will be unable to use the shop and receive half the experience points from mining the stars.

==Locating==
[[File:Shooting Stars - telescope view.png|thumb|300px|A shooting star viewed through a telescope.]]
Members can use a [[Telescope space|telescope]] in a [[Study|study room]] in a [[player-owned house]] to find the approximate area and time of the next landing. It is also possible to use telescopes in another player's house for this purpose.
* If the telescope is blocked by another room in the house, (not including outdoor rooms such as the [[Menagerie]]), or the room is underground, it will not work.
* Better telescopes provide a more accurate time window:
** [[Oak telescope]] - 24-minute window
** [[Teak telescope]] - 9-minute window
** [[Mahogany telescope]] - 2-minute window
* If a star has recently fallen, the following text appears:
** "You look through the telescope but you don't see anything interesting."
Join the Shooting Stars [[grouping]] chat via the grouping menu to share locations with other players. 

There are also many websites available on the internet which list known star sites allowing players to quickly find stars meeting their criteria.

If a player is standing near the crash site where a shooting star is falling, they will hear a whistling sound as it falls from the sky and the crash as it impacts the ground.

==Mining==
[[File:Shooting Star crashing.gif|frame|A shooting star crashing.]]

[[Crashed stars]] may be mined through a number of layers before they will be fully depleted.  Each layer will '''always''' deplete at a fixed rate of 7 minutes, provided there is at least one player mining it. On first appearance, stars will range in size from 6 to 9 layers, and the star will crumble and disappear once the final layer has been mined. Only one star may be active at a time on any given world; the previous star will disappear if another star appears before it is fully depleted. {{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1392938928341200901|date=13 May 2021|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20210513202538/https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1392938928341200901|archivedate=13 May 2021|quote=[do shooting stars reset if not being mined?] Looks to me like an old star would be deleted at the time when the next spawns, if it hasn't already gone.}}

Each layer has an associated [[Mining]] level requirement, decreasing with each layer that is mined through. Players can find out how large the star is by prospecting it, which will also reveal the percentage progress towards depleting the current layer.

While mining the crashed star, a roll to receive stardust is performed regularly based on the player's [[Mining]] level, scaling from 29% to 46% at levels 1 to 99. Players will additionally receive 32 (32.8 with the full [[Prospector kit|prospectors kit]]) experience each time a piece of stardust is mined (halved to 16 on Free-to-play worlds). [[Mining enhancers]] that multiply yield do '''not''' affect stars.

{{Listen
|title = [[Star of Your Own (Shooting Stars)|Star of Your Own]]
|align = right
|filename = Star of Your Own (Shooting Stars).ogg
|desc = The jingle that plays upon discovering a crashed star.}}

There is a star discovery bonus available to the first player that attempts to mine a crashed star, who will receive double stardust for the next 300 mined from '''any''' shooting star. Experience is '''not''' doubled. This bonus persists through logouts and server updates, and will reset to 300 if another star is discovered while the bonus is active. You do not need to meet the skill requirements for the layer to receive the bonus. 

In addition to receiving this bonus, their name will be added to the [[Shooting Star Noticeboard]] in the reception room north of the [[Observatory]], which records the last five players to discover stars on the server.

It is possible to receive the pet [[rock golem]] whilst mining, where the base chance is 1/521,550.

===Notes===
*The shooting star cycle will reset during a system update; stars on the ground before the update will vanish. Stars will begin landing again 20–50 minutes after the game goes back online, and then cycle as normal (every ~90 minutes)
*It is possible that the telescopes of two POH will show different timers. In such a case, the landing time can be narrowed down to the time when the timers overlap. For example, if one telescope says a star is 10-12 minutes from landing and another says 9-11 minutes, the star must be 10-11 minutes from landing.
*The [[adamant pickaxe]]'s 4-[[tick]] cycle allows it to be used for [[tick manipulation]] while mining shooting stars, unlike other pickaxes.
*Gems are able to be obtained from mining stars. A charged [[amulet of glory]] will increase this rate. A [[gem bag]] or [[gem sack]] may be worth bringing, or a [[chisel]] to craft [[bolt tips]].
*In [[Varlamore]], crashed stars can reward the [[Loop half of key (moon key)]].
*When attempting to mine a star you do not have the required level for, it is possible to degrade the star by up to 1% even though you are unable to mine it for stardust. This may be done every 7 ticks, and is a result of the check for the remaining time on a star occuring earlier than the check for the required level. This is not affected by other players.

==Landing sites==
Members may make use of a [[Telescope space|telescope]] to reveal the general area in which the star will fall, wherein there are a number of set locations in which the star may land. A star will not land in the same spot twice in a row.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1469848696179376128|date=12 December 2021|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/100596|archivedate=25 April 2023|quote=If I'm reading the code correctly, it rolls randomly from a list that *excludes* this Darkmeyer spot. And if it rolls the same place it used before, it'll instead go to this spot.}}

The only way to locate the actual crash site is to search each possible crash site in the given area until the [[Crashed Star|crashed star]] is found; this process, as well as the mining process, can be greatly expedited with the assistance of other players.

There are a total of 82 possible landing sites, 21 of which are located in free-to-play areas. Stars may land in members areas on free-to-play worlds.

Some crash site areas contain aggressive mobs; low level players should take care when selecting a star location to mine at, especially if they do not intend to pay attention while mining. Star locations contained within cities are typically safe.

==Changes==
{{Subject changes header}}
{{Subject changes
|date = 25 October 2023
|update = Forestry: Part Two
|change = * [[Crashed star]]s will now only spawn sizes 6 to 9, with updated chances of spawning for each.
* The total time of each "wave" of stars has been reduced from ~128 minutes to ~90 minutes.
* Crashed stars now consistently deplete at a rate of 7 minutes for each layer it has.
* Mining experience gained when acquiring stardust has been changed to be 32 for all star sizes.
* The [[skilling success rate]] whilst mining crashed stars is now identical for all star sizes.
* [[Clue geode]]s are once again obtainable from crashed stars.
* [[Crystal shard]]s are no longer obtainable from crashed stars that land in [[Prifddinas]].
* [[Random event]]s and the [[dwarf multicannon]] can no longer occur and be placed within the vicinity of a landing site.
}}
{{Subject changes
|date = 2 October 2023
|type = hotfix
|change = Receiving clue geodes from crashed stars has been disabled in an effort to help server performance.{{CiteTwitter|author=Old School RuneScape|date=2 October 2023|url=https://twitter.com/OldSchoolRS/status/1708861719051661384|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/98812|archivedate=2 October 2023|quote=As an initial measure to help server performance, we've disabled the ability for players to receive Clue Geodes from mining Shooting Stars.}}
}}
{{Subject changes
|date = 20 September 2023
|update = Poll 80 & Shooting Stars Changes
|change = * [[Crashed star]]s no longer deplete faster when more people are mining them.
* Player characters will no longer occasionally render behind the crashed star they are mining.
}}
{{Subject changes
|date = 10 November 2021
|update = Wilderness & Small Changes
|change = Shooting Stars now have a chance to land in Darkmeyer, as previously intended.
}}
{{Subject changes
|date = 30 June 2021
|update = Phosani's Nightmare
|poll = A Night At The Theatre and Old School Content Poll 75: PvM
|change = Experience from mining crashed stars have been increased per stardust mined.
}}
{{Subject changes
|date = 24 March 2021
|update = Fishing Skill Boss and Easter Event
|change = *Shooting Stars should now deplete more slowly when large groups are mining them.
*Cannons can once again be placed where a Shooting Star would land. However, if a Star lands on it, it will be destroyed and will need to be reclaimed from Nulodion.
*There is now a chance players might receive additional stardust when mining Shooting Stars.
}}
{{Subject changes
|date = 17 March 2021
|type = hotfix
|change = Players with the Twisted, Hosidius, and Cosy Cabin house styles can now properly use the telescope.
}}
{{Subject changes footer}}

==Historical==
As a piece of content brought into ''Old School RuneScape'' via [[backporting]], Shooting Stars were originally released on 2 September 2008 in ''RuneScape 3'' as one of three {{RSL|Distractions and Diversions}}, alongside {{RSL|Balthazar Beauregard's Big Top Bonanza}} and {{RSL|Penguin Hide and Seek}}.

Like most content backported into ''Old School RuneScape'', the Shooting Stars for ''Old School'' has a few differences which aim to better adapt it for ''Old School RuneScape''.
*''RuneScape 3'' has 44 possible landing sites; ''Old School RuneScape'' has 82.
*Originally, Shooting Stars were only available for [[members]]. This was changed on 9 October 2017 in ''RuneScape 3''.
**On free-to-play worlds, Shooting Stars may crash in a members area, rendering it out of reach.
**Mining experience on free-to-play servers is half that of on members servers.
*There is no additional experience given for the first player to mine the fallen star.
*Players receive a reduced amount of experience per stardust.
* In ''RuneScape 3,'' players could hold only up to 200 stardust, and could only exchange it once per day. ''Old School RuneScape'' does not have either of these limits.
*[[Star Sprite]]s do not exist in ''Old School RuneScape''; rewards are exchanged for stardust via a shop run by Dusuri instead.
